title: Meeting people
summary: You already know plenty of words. This unit gives them a skeleton: how to say what something is, isn't, and whose it is.
canDo: I can introduce myself and say where I'm from.
I can ask and answer simple yes/no questions about people and things.
I can say what something is and who or what it belongs to.
grammar: はい、そうです・いいえ、ちがいます

items.back: A is B. は (said "wa") marks the topic; です makes the sentence polite.
items.note: レオさん{は|wa}{学生|がくせい}です。 Leo is a student.

items.back: A is not B (polite, spoken). More formal: ではありません.
items.note: {学生|がくせい}じゃありません。 I'm not a student.

items.back: Add か to make a question. Word order does not change.
items.note: ブラジル{人|じん}ですか。 Are you Brazilian?

items.back: Nice to meet you (only at a first meeting).

items.front: よろしくお{願|ねが}いします
items.back: Closing line of an introduction: "pleased to meet you / I look forward to getting on with you".
"I see" / "Is that so?" With falling intonation it simply shows you are listening.
office worker, company employee
B of A / A's B. The word that describes or owns comes first.
items.note: {東京|とうきょう}のチーム a Tokyo team

items.back: A too. も takes the place of は.
items.note: わたしもサッカーファンです。 I'm a football fan too.

items.back: this (near me) · that (near you) · that over there (far from both of us)
What is it?

items.front: この・その・あの + noun
items.back: this ~ (near me) · that ~ (near you) · that ~ over there. They must be followed by a noun; これ・それ・あれ stand alone.
"It's mine." After の the noun can be dropped when it is obvious.
items.note: あの{人|ひと}のです。 It's that person's.

items.back: whose
items.note: だれの{傘|かさ}ですか。 Whose umbrella is it?

items.back: "Well then" / "in that case". Casual; the neutral form is では.

items.front: どこ・だれ・{何|なん} + ですか
items.back: where · who · what. The question word sits exactly where the answer will go; nothing moves to the front.
items.note: お{国|くに}{は|wa}どこですか。 → ブラジルです。

items.front: お{国|くに}{は|wa}どこですか
items.back: Where are you from? (literally: your country is where?) Politer: どちらですか.

items.front: お{仕事|しごと}{は|wa}{何|なん}ですか
items.back: What do you do for work?

items.front: ブラジルから{来|き}ました
items.back: I'm from Brazil (I came from Brazil). Swap in any country. Learn it as a set phrase for now; verbs come in the next unit.
items.note: {日本|にほん}から{来|き}ました。 I'm from Japan.

items.back: "And you, ~?" Name + は with rising intonation sends the same question back.
Polite prefix for things that belong to the other person: お{国|くに}, お{仕事|しごと}, お{名前|なまえ}. Don't use it for your own.
Yes, that's right. The standard short "yes" to a noun question.
No, that's not right. Softer than repeating じゃありません.
Excuse me / sorry. The normal way to get someone's attention.
Self-introduction. The usual order: はじめまして → name → where from → job → よろしくお{願|ねが}いします.

lessons.title: A is B: は and です
lessons.canDo: I can say who I am, say what I'm not, and ask a yes/no question.

intro.scene: A hostel lounge. Leo, a traveller from Brazil, meets Nakamura-san.

lines.text: はじめまして。{中村|なかむら}です。
lines.meaning: Nice to meet you. I'm Nakamura.

lines.text: はじめまして。レオです。ブラジル{人|じん}です。
lines.meaning: Nice to meet you. I'm Leo. I'm Brazilian.

lines.text: レオさん{は|wa}{学生|がくせい}ですか。
いいえ、{学生|がくせい}じゃありません。{会社員|かいしゃいん}です。
lines.meaning: No, I'm not a student. I'm an office worker.

lines.text: そうですか。よろしくお{願|ねが}いします。
lines.meaning: I see. Pleased to meet you.

notes.title: A{は|wa}Bです
notes.body: {は|wa} marks what you are talking about (the topic) and is pronounced "wa" here. です closes the sentence politely. Japanese has no "a/the" and no verb changes for I/you/he.

notes.title: Drop what is obvious
notes.body: Leo says レオです, not わたし{は|wa}レオです. When the topic is clear, Japanese leaves it out. Repeating わたし{は|wa} in every sentence sounds unnatural.

notes.title: Not B, and questions
notes.body: じゃありません = "is not". Add か to です for a question: ですか. Use the other person's name + さん where English says "you".

lessons.title: Whose, which, and "too": の, も, これ・それ・あれ
lessons.canDo: I can ask what something is, link two nouns with の, and say "me too".

intro.scene: Same lounge. Leo has something in his hand.

lines.text: それ{は|wa}{何|なん}ですか。
これですか。サッカーのチケットです。
{日本|にほん}のチームですか。
はい、{東京|とうきょう}のチームです。
わたしもサッカーファンです。

notes.title: AのB
notes.body: の links two nouns. The describing or owning word comes first: サッカーのチケット (football ticket), レオさんのチケット (Leo's ticket). The order is the reverse of Portuguese "ingresso de futebol".

notes.title: も = too
notes.body: も replaces {は|wa}: わたし{は|wa} → わたしも. Never {は|wa}も.

notes.title: これ・それ・あれ
notes.body: これ is near the speaker, それ is near the listener, あれ is far from both. That is why Nakamura says それ and Leo answers これ about the same ticket.

intro.scene: By the lounge door there is an umbrella nobody has claimed.

lines.text: この{傘|かさ}{は|wa}レオさんのですか。
いいえ、わたしのじゃありません。
じゃあ、だれの{傘|かさ}ですか。
あの{人|ひと}のです。
そうですか。ありがとうございます。

notes.title: この vs これ
notes.body: これ・それ・あれ stand alone: これ{は|wa}{傘|かさ}です. この・その・あの need a noun right after them: この{傘|かさ}. Portuguese uses one word for both ("este" / "este guarda-chuva"); Japanese does not.

notes.title: 〜のです = mine, yours, theirs
notes.body: After の you can drop a noun that is obvious: わたしの{傘|かさ}です → わたしのです (it's mine). あの{人|ひと}のです = it's that person's.

notes.title: だれの
notes.body: だれ = who, so だれの = whose. Like every question word, it stays where the answer goes: だれの{傘|かさ}ですか → あの{人|ひと}の{傘|かさ}です.

exercises.prompt: Fill the gap.

notes.title: Question words stay put
notes.body: English moves the question word to the front. Japanese leaves it where the answer goes: お{国|くに}{は|wa}どこですか → お{国|くに}{は|wa}ブラジルです. Swap the word, keep the sentence.

notes.title: お〜 is for the other person
notes.body: お{国|くに}, お{仕事|しごと}, お{名前|なまえ} show respect for what belongs to the listener. Talking about yourself, drop it: {仕事|しごと}{は|wa}{会社員|かいしゃいん}です.

notes.title: 〜さん{は|wa}？
notes.body: To return a question, say the name + {は|wa} with rising intonation. No need to repeat the whole question.

notes.title: 〜から{来|き}ました
notes.body: "I came from ~". Treat it as a ready-made phrase for now. Verbs like {来|き}ます get their own unit next.

notes.title: はい、そうです · いいえ、ちがいます
notes.body: The everyday short answers to "is it X?" questions. そうです = "that's so". ちがいます = "that's different", a gentler no than repeating じゃありません.

notes.title: すみません
notes.body: "Excuse me" to start talking to a stranger, and also a light "sorry". You will use it constantly in Japan.

notes.title: Your self-introduction
notes.body: The usual order: はじめまして。→ name + です。→ place + から{来|き}ました。→ job + です。→ よろしくお{願|ねが}いします。 Short sentences, no わたし{は|wa} needed.
